newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares fall on IMF, Surgutneftegaz news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares fall on IMF, Surgutneftegaz news.

text.p: Leading shares fell on Thursday on Russia's failure to reach agreement with the International Monetary Fund on a new loan tranche and Surgut Holding's increased stake in Surgutneftegaz via a closed share issue, traders said.
They forecast a further fall in prices.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 1.22 percent to 185.28 on $23.58 million in volume.
"Investors were upset," said Alexander Bubnovsky, head of sales at IK Alfa-Capital. "Those who wanted to buy, suspended orders."
The central bank said on Thursday that a team from the IMF would leave Moscow without reaching a conclusion on whether to give Russia the latest tranche of a three-year $10 billion loan.
Bubnovsky said the IMF news came about the time when New York opened and "spoiled investors' mood."

He said the disappointment about the IMF news coincided with a decision by some operators' to start taking profits after a rise generated by the oversubscription of Gazprom's American Depositary Share issue..
"The market today is mur," Bubnovsky said.
Dismay about the IMF came on top of the news that Surgut Holding had raised its stake in Surgutneftegaz to 43.5 percent from 38 percent by acquiring a new share issue.

"After that news investors who temporarily forgot about main risks in Russia, about the fact that minority shareholders' interests are not taken into consideration, remembered about them again," Bubunovsky said.
Surgutneftegaz fell to $0.428 from $0.462 on Wednesday's close.

Andrei Kukk, chief trader at Rinaco-Plus, said the IMF news coupled with the gossip about a possible sacking of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, which was later denied, had a very negative impact on prices.
"This news pushed the market down strongly and will push it down more," he said, forecasting a five to six percent fall in the next few days.
However, he said Surgutneftegaz could only fall by a further two percent, as the share fell strongly on Thursday.
Mosenergo was traded at $0.946 after $0.985, Rostelekom edged down to $2.60 from $2.73 and UES was $0.0816 after $0.0850. Gazprom fell to $0.510 from $0.515.
